evals.prompt: PM wants to A/B test a completely new review experience next sprint: new layout, new recommendations, new prompts, all at once, judged on conversion after two weeks. Advise.
evals.expected_output: A response that reframes this as a foundation release: staged rollout with a guardrails-only backlash check first, stabilization, then separate experiments per change with one primary metric each.
expectations: Distinguishes foundation releases from optimization experiments
First stage reads guardrails only, not a win metric
Rejects judging multiple simultaneous changes with one two-week conversion test

evals.prompt: Day 5 of a planned 21-day test, p=0.04 in favor of the variant. The team wants to ship now. What do you say?
evals.expected_output: A response that explains peeking inflates false positives, insists on the pre-committed sample/duration, and offers sequential testing as the legitimate path to early stopping.
expectations: Refuses early stopping based on an interim p-value
Explains inflated false-positive risk from peeking
Mentions sequential testing as the valid alternative

evals.prompt: We ran out of users to test on, so we plan to reuse the control group from a running experiment for a second one. Thoughts?
evals.expected_output: A response that treats capacity as a hard constraint, warns against manual control-group sharing (invalid isolation, high bug risk), and points to platform namespaces or waiting for a free slot.
expectations: Frames experiment capacity as a physical constraint to plan around
Recommends platform-native mutual exclusivity (namespaces) or sequencing tests

evals.prompt: Our experiment on per-question hint styles counts every user assigned at page load, but most never open a hint. Results look flat. Diagnose.
evals.expected_output: A response that identifies assignment-vs-exposure dilution and moves exposure logging to the render point of the hint.
expectations: Identifies that assigned-but-never-exposed users dilute the measured effect
Recommends firing exposure at the component/render point for item-level experiments
